summary.text: 第 is conventionally analyzed as 竹 “bamboo” plus 弟, which plausibly cues its pronunciation. Its central meaning is “sequence” or “order”; today it commonly precedes a numeral to mark an ordinal. How these uses developed is unresolved.

formation.text: The received form is conventionally analyzed as phonosemantic: 竹 contributes a bamboo-related category, and 弟 plausibly cues the sound. The bamboo element has been linked to writing strips, but that explanation is not established as the graph’s original motivation. Some historical accounts say 第 was once written 弟 alone or that 弟 was shortened in a common form; neither establishes when or how the graphic change occurred. Another account calls 第 pictographic, and the descriptions do not resolve the disagreement.

components.text: ⺮ is the positional side form of 竹, “bamboo,” and contributes a bamboo-related category in 第. Its proposed connection with writing strips is not established as the graph’s original motivation.

弟 is the phonetic element in the received-form analysis. Historical accounts say 第 may once have been written 弟 alone, or that 弟 was shortened in a common form, but they do not establish the timing or exact graphic change.

sound_limitation.text: The sound comparison supports a plausible phonetic role, but does not identify 弟’s earliest referent or recover its original spoken name.

sound.text: Modern Mandarin and Cantonese readings match. Zhengzhang gives related Old Chinese forms with different final marking; Baxter–Sagart likewise gives related forms with different final and tone marking.
sound.component_reading: dì; Cantonese dai6; Old Chinese Zhengzhang *diːlʔ; Baxter–Sagart *lˤəjʔ (younger-brother reading)
sound.character_reading: dì; Cantonese dai6; Old Chinese Zhengzhang *diːls; Baxter–Sagart *[l]ˤəjʔ-s
sound.system: Modern Mandarin and Cantonese; Old Chinese Zhengzhang (2003) and Baxter–Sagart (2014)

history.text: Historical-form indexes list oracle-bone, bronze, manuscript, seal, and clerical categories, but do not show or analyze individual 第 forms. The suggestion that 第 was originally written 弟 remains undated; the available accounts do not establish a sequence of graphic changes.

uncertainties.text: The bamboo-writing explanation is proposed, not demonstrated by early forms. Accounts differ between calling 第 pictographic and analyzing it as 竹 plus 弟; the available descriptions do not resolve the discrepancy.
弟 is a plausible phonetic component, but its earliest referent and original name are not recovered. The proposed connection with 梯 and language-specific contraction accounts are uncorroborated here.

senses.text: Dictionary accounts give the meaning “sequence” or “order,” but the earliest attestation is unsettled: one quotation has 第，次也, while an inspected transcription has 弟，次也. The text’s composition date and witness history are unresolved.
第 commonly precedes a numeral to mark an ordinal. The first occurrence of this use is not dated here.

senses.period: Han text example; broader dating unresolved
senses.text: A Han Shu passage uses 第 for ranking performances. Dictionary accounts also record examination rank and evaluation; these uses do not establish the graph’s original meaning.
A text dated 815 uses 第 to refer to the time after passing an examination. How this use developed from sequence or rank is unresolved.
Dictionary accounts record a residence sense and give a rank-related explanation, but its date and development are unresolved.
Dictionary accounts record an adverbial “only” or “just” sense. Its history and any relation to “sequence” are unresolved.

limitations.text: The links among sequence, ordinal marking, ranking, examination success, residence, and “only/just” are not established, so these senses are presented separately rather than as a semantic chain.
The earliest sequence attestation is unsettled: one dictionary quotation gives 第, while the inspected 小爾雅 transcription gives 弟. The text’s composition date and witness history are unresolved.

overview.text: 第 combines a bamboo-related element with 弟 as a plausible sound cue. It means “sequence” or “order” and commonly marks an ordinal before a numeral; how these uses relate historically is unresolved.

components.text: ⺮ is the positional side form of 竹, “bamboo,” and contributes a bamboo-related category. Its connection with writing strips is only a proposed explanation.
弟 is a plausible sound cue: it matches 第 in modern Mandarin and Cantonese, while Old Chinese reconstructions share a sound base but differ in final or tone marking.

relationships.text: The received-form analysis assigns the bamboo side form a semantic role in 第.
Modern and reconstructed readings support 弟 as a plausible phonetic component in 第, though 弟’s earliest referent and name remain unrecovered.
